title: WPA Global Institutions Master List — REV4 Coverage Expansion Candidate

baseline.rule: REV3 remains the frozen reproducible baseline until each REV4 candidate passes entity resolution, source verification and authorised human review.

purpose: Systematically close global coverage gaps in diplomatic academies, foreign-service institutes, protocol schools and closely related diplomatic-training institutions. Candidate presence in this file does not create canonical inclusion, accreditation, endorsement or a ranking result.

discovery_sources.name: International Forum on Diplomatic Training (IFDT) Directory
discovery_sources.role: discovery/control list only; institutional facts should be confirmed through primary or authoritative sources where reasonably available

discovery_sources.name: National ministries of foreign affairs and official institutional sites

candidate_wave_1.name: MFA Diplomatic Academy
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Singapore MFA states that the Diplomatic Academy was established on 1 February 2007 and runs structured professional development for diplomats and officials.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic Academy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Serbian MFA documents the Academy's institutional history, diplomatic-consular training, pre-posting preparation, professional exams and specialist programmes.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic Academy
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Montenegro's Ministry of Foreign Affairs identifies the Academy as an organisational unit for training diplomats and public servants representing the country abroad.

candidate_wave_1.name: Hennadii Udovenko Diplomatic Academy of Ukraine at the MFA
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Ukraine MFA describes the Academy as a state postgraduate educational and research institution created in 1995 for diplomatic-service and international-relations professional training.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic Academy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Polish MFA documents induction, career-diplomat, pre-posting, language, diplomatic-consular examination and international training functions.

candidate_wave_1.name: Foreign Service Academy
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Kenyan MFA documents the transition from Foreign Service Institute to Academy in 2017 and its training, research and institutional-capacity mandate.

candidate_wave_1.name: Instituto Matías Romero
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Mexico's government identifies Instituto Matías Romero as the diplomatic academy of Mexico, created in 1974 by the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs. Existing A006 requires entity-resolution review before any additional record is created.

candidate_wave_1.name: Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: AGDA describes itself as a diplomatic academic institute providing education, training and policy research; it states that it was licensed by the UAE Ministry of Education and Commission for Academic Accreditation in 2015.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic Institute, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Qatar MFA assigns the Institute diplomatic and consular training, mission-personnel development, research and policy-analysis functions.

candidate_wave_1.name: Institute of Diplomacy and Foreign Relations (IDFR)
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: IDFR identifies itself as the Malaysian MFA training institute operating since 1991, with diplomatic training, international capacity building and specialised centres.

candidate_wave_1.name: Foreign Service Academy
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Pakistan MFA identifies FSA as its training arm, established in 1981, providing entry-level, mid-career and international diplomatic training.

candidate_wave_1.name: Foreign Service Academy
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Bangladesh MFA states that FSA was established in 1996 for specialised training of Bangladesh Foreign Service officers.

candidate_wave_1.name: Foreign Service Institute
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: The Philippine FSI publicly documents a diplomacy school, strategic-studies centre, publications, evaluation and institutional governance functions.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic Academy, Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Croatia's MFA lists dedicated departments for diplomatic training and lifelong learning, pre-deployment training, academic development and international cooperation.

candidate_wave_1.name: Hellenic Diplomatic Academy
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Greek MFA states that HDA was founded in 1999 and provides initial professional training, continuing MFA training and student internships.

candidate_wave_1.name: Mohamed bin Mubarak Al Khalifa Academy for Diplomatic Studies
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: The Academy states that it was established by Royal Decree on 1 August 2019, succeeding the MFA Diplomatic Institute, with training, research, outreach and global-partnership functions.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic Academy, Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Slovenian government identifies the Head of the Diplomatic Academy and documents diplomatic, higher diplomatic and consular examination/training activity.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic School of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Armenian MFA documents the Diplomatic School, its International Relations and Diplomacy programme, graduates and continuing international cooperation; MFA history states the school has operated since 2009.

candidate_wave_1.name: ADA University — School of Public and International Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: ADA University offers Diplomacy and International Affairs and International Relations programmes. Its official academic catalogue identifies the University as the legal heir of the Azerbaijan Diplomatic Academy founded in 2006.

candidate_wave_1.name: Diplomatic Institute to the Minister of Foreign Affairs
candidate_wave_1.evidence_note: Bulgarian MFA describes the Diplomatic Institute as a leading institution for diplomatic training, professional qualification, international cooperation and contemporary diplomatic practice.

human_gate: No candidate changes the canonical Master List until an authorised reviewer confirms identity, source quality, duplicate/successor status, group classification and correction-ready provenance.
